findings.reason: as written, done-when case 4 asserts a release the mechanism cannot produce for a same-session pair, so a builder testing the case as worded gets a failing gate and either widens the mechanism (moving the pre-check above the allowance check) or drops a requirement the section states.
findings.text: the added paragraph bounds the overlap hold by STARVATION_AGE_SECONDS and motivates it with "The earlier request may itself be held without end, for example when its session is never granted a slot", but when the two overlapping requests sit in that same slot-less session the later one is held by the session-allowance check in admit_once (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:571, `if allowance is not None and allowance <= 0: result["held"].append(...); continue`), which runs before the pre-check, so the pre-check never sees it and the escape never fires; the hold is then unbounded, which is the exact pathology the cited §4 measurement (c-s4-head-of-queue-starved) records

findings.reason: without an arm that removes the escape and requires the later request to stay queued, the section cannot demonstrate the guard it adds, which is how a guard that never fires ships.
findings.text: the release-at-starvation-age case declares no control, and neither declared control can falsify it: removing the admission pre-check makes the later request reach the launch path and launch anyway (the earlier request is a queued pointer, which under mechanism 1 no longer binds), and re-counting queued pointers as binding likewise leaves the later request launching, so the case passes in both arms and the escape's firing is never shown load-bearing

findings.reason: the ordering exists in one direction only; §15 built first recreates the admission loop §18 then rewrites, and the plan's own convention is that the later section states its predecessors.
findings.text: §18 states "This section runs after §14 ... and before §15, which also writes queue_admission.py", but §15's own text declares "runs after §9, §10, §11 and §14, which also write these files" and does not name §18, and §15 is implementable now, so a coordinator dispatching §15 has no signal that §18 must precede it

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — claim_disposition (reckon/crew/node.py:1450), _repository_scope_claims (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:222), _live_scope_claims (reckon/crew/runs.py:856), _require_launched_record (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:514) and STARVATION_AGE_SECONDS = 30 * 60 (reckon/crew/queue_order.py:13) all resolve, the superseded test exists at tests/test_a_node_is_queued_once.py:307 with exactly the shape §18 describes, and every extensionless href resolves with .html appended (each anchor checked against docs/evidence/archive/a-held-dispatch-waits-its-fair-turn-landed.html).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the starvation-release case added on line 135 names no control, and neither of the two declared controls can falsify it, so no arm shows the release guard firing.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both negative-control logs sit under the run directory and no gate, base arm or evidence path named on line 135 is a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the changed text adds no plan label, stage name, ticket number or changelog prose; it names real symbols (STARVATION_AGE_SECONDS, claim_disposition, admit_once) and states the mechanism.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the starvation bound added on line 135 cannot bound the hold in the same-session case the same sentence raises as its motivation, because the session-allowance hold fires before the pre-check.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the two mechanisms are one contract (a queued claim refuses no launch, and rank order among overlapping queued requests is kept), each with its own control; splitting would cost a node and a review for one invariant.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §18 declares it runs before §15 (line 135), but §15's own ordering list names §9, §10, §11 and §14 and omits §18, while both write reckon/crew/queue_admission.py and §15 is implementable now.
